Regional association plot for coloc results

plot_coloc_regional.Rd

Plots -log10(p) against position, with exposure and outcome panels. Points are coloured by LD (r2) with an index SNP, using the r2 stored by run_coloc(), so no PLINK or panel is needed at plot time. With no stored r2 (a run_coloc() call with no bfile, or an object saved before mrpipeline 0.10.0), passing bfile computes it for this plot, and otherwise the plot is uncoloured, with any recorded index SNP still marked.

Usage

plot_coloc_regional(
  x,
  ens_db = NULL,
  bfile = NULL,
  plink_bin = NULL,
  index_snp = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A coloc_result object.

ens_db

NULL (the default) for no gene track, or an ensembldb::EnsDb object, or the name of an Ensembl annotation package as a string (e.g. "EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75"), matching the genome build of x's data. If given as a string, the package must be attached first (library(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75)), not merely installed.

bfile

Path to PLINK bfile prefix (without .bed/.bim/.fam), the local LD reference panel. Only used when r2 has to be computed: x has no stored r2, or index_snp differs from the stored index SNP. SNPs absent from the panel stay on the plot in grey.

plink_bin

Path to PLINK binary. If NULL, auto-detected via genetics.binaRies::get_plink_binary().

index_snp

rsID to colour LD against, overriding any index SNP stored by run_coloc() for this plot. Defaults to the stored index SNP, or the exposure lead when there is none: the lowest pval.exposure, with ties going to the largest |beta/se|. Must be one of the SNPs in x.

...

Forwarded to compute_ld_to_index() (plink_threads, plink_memory).

Value

A ggplot object, or NULL invisibly if there is no harmonised data.

Details

The same index SNP and r2 are used in both panels, so the outcome panel shows LD with the exposure lead by default, not with the outcome lead.

With ens_db, a gene track from locuszoomr is added under the panels, the x axis is in Mb rather than bp, and the plots are composed with cowplot::plot_grid(). Adding ggplot2::labs(title = ...) still sets the title, but other ggplot2 additions, such as theme() changes to the panels, do not reach a composed plot.
